about.title: Personal Injury Help in Rosemead, California
about.longDescription: Rosemead's streets carry heavy daily traffic, from Walnut Grove Avenue and Garvey Avenue to Valley Boulevard and the I-10 San Bernardino Freeway corridor that cuts through town. Public records show 216 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, leaving 275 people hurt and 3 people dead. Many of these crashes cluster around Friday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m., when commuter traffic is heaviest. If you or someone you love was hurt in one of these collisions, sorting out medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls can feel overwhelming on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured Rosemead residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened. Attorneys in this network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover money on your behalf. There's no obligation to move forward, and reaching out costs you nothing. Getting informed early, before evidence disappears or deadlines pass, can make a real difference in how your case is handled.

items.title: You Have a Limited Window
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government entity can require notice in as little as six months. Acting sooner helps preserve your options.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the incident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. An attorney can help make sure this part of your claim isn't overlooked.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in this network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they win or settle your case. That means you can get legal help without worrying about hourly bills.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Rosemead?
items.answer: California law generally gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, such as a city vehicle, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's important not to wait.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Rosemead?
items.answer: Public crash records show higher collision counts along Walnut Grove Avenue, Garvey Avenue, Valley Boulevard, and near the I-10 freeway corridor. These are simply the corridors with the highest recorded volume of collisions, not a judgment about any specific location.

items.question: Is there a cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney; we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so you don't pay unless they recover money for you.

items.question: What kind of compensation might be available?
items.answer: Depending on the facts, compensation can include medical expenses, lost wages, and pain and suffering, which California does not cap in ordinary injury cases. An attorney can review your specific situation to explain what may apply.
